# Hashed, pinned dependency set for pipeline-execution-parity-ci.yml ONLY.
#
# Generated 2026-07-14 by resolving/downloading each package below as a
# manylinux2014/manylinux_2_17/manylinux_2_28 x86_64 cp311 wheel (matching
# the runner: ubuntu-latest + actions/setup-python@v5 python-version "3.11")
# via:
#
#   pip download --dest wheels-linux-cp311 \
#     --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 --platform manylinux_2_17_x86_64 \
#     --platform manylinux_2_28_x86_64 --python-version 311 \
#     --implementation cp --abi cp311 --only-binary=:all: \
#     "arch>=6.3,<8" "numpy>=1.24,<3.0" "pandas>=2.0,<3.0" \
#     "pandas_market_calendars>=4,<5" "pyarrow>=14.0,<26" \
#     "pydantic>=2.0,<3.0" "scipy>=1.10,<2.0" "statsmodels>=0.14,<1.0" \
#     "requests>=2.31,<3.0" "cvxpy>=1.4,<2.0" "pytest>=7.4,<9.0"
#
# then sha256-hashing every downloaded wheel. Direct (top-level) packages are
# arch, numpy, pandas, pandas_market_calendars, pyarrow, pydantic, scipy,
# statsmodels, requests, cvxpy, pytest; everything else here is a transitive
# dependency of those. All packages -- direct and transitive -- must be
# listed with a hash for `pip install --require-hashes` to succeed; that is
# also why this pins exact versions rather than ranges (a hash only matches
# one exact artifact).
#
# The `<3.0` / `<8` ceilings on pandas/arch (and the pre-existing `<5` on
# pandas_market_calendars, `<3.0` on pydantic) are deliberate: they keep this
# CI job on the same major-version line already validated elsewhere in this
# repo's own dev environment (see `requirements.lock.txt`,
# `environment.yml`), rather than silently picking up an unproven new major
# release the moment PyPI publishes one -- pandas 3.0 in particular is a
# breaking major bump over the 2.x line renquant-pipeline/renquant-execution
# are actually developed and tested against.
#
# Verified by installing this file with `pip install --require-hashes` in a
# clean `python:3.11-slim` (linux/amd64) container; see
# doc/progress/2026-07-13-g3-a2-a3-pipeline-execution-parity-ci.md
# ("Codex hardening follow-up" section) for the full verification record,
# including a disclosed QEMU-emulation caveat on cross-arch import checks.
#
# To regenerate: bump the version ceilings above if a deliberate upgrade is
# wanted, re-run the `pip download` command in a clean venv, sha256sum each
# wheel, and replace the body below. Do not hand-edit a version or hash.
